Job Description
The Software Quality Assurance Analyst is Pedros’ internal software-quality specialist, responsible for establishing and executing structured, independent quality assurance and testing practices across the Group’s technology and digital transformation projects. The role ensures that software applications, integrations, workflows, reports and digital solutions meet approved business requirements, operate reliably across interconnected systems and are sufficiently stable for implementation.
Reporting to the Group Project Manager, the role works closely with project managers, business analysts, developers, vendors and business stakeholders to identify quality risks, develop test strategies, execute testing, manage defects and support User Acceptance Testing. It supports web and mobile applications, internally developed systems, vendor solutions, Microsoft Power Platform applications, POS integrations, transactional platforms, reporting solutions and operational systems across Pedros and its associated brands.
The role establishes consistent QA standards, templates, quality gates and reporting, giving project teams and decision-makers clear visibility of test coverage, open defects, quality risks and release readiness before systems are implemented.
Responsibilities :
Test Execution, Integration & Transactional Testing
Execute manual functional, system, integration, end-to-end, regression, smoke, sanity, usability and compatibility testing across relevant browsers, devices, operating systems and user roles
Test integrations between internal systems, vendor platforms, APIs, POS systems, payment services, databases, Microsoft 365 services and reporting platforms
Validate successful and unsuccessful transaction paths (error handling, retries, timeouts, cancellations, duplicates), data synchronisation and reconciliation outputs, with particular focus on financial, voucher, payment and loyalty flows.
Record test results with supporting evidence and perform exploratory testing to identify issues not covered by predefined test cases.
Quality Assurance Strategy, Planning & Standards
Develop and maintain test strategies, test plans and schedules, defining scope, test types, environments, dependencies, risks and entry and exit criteria for each testing cycle
Apply risk-based testing principles to prioritise high-impact business processes, financial transactions, security controls, integrations and customer-facing functionality
Estimate testing effort and provide realistic input into project plans, sprint plans and release schedules.
Requirements Review & Test Design
Review requirements, user stories, process maps, business rules and acceptance criteria to confirm they are clear, complete, consistent and testable
Identify gaps, ambiguities, edge cases, control weaknesses and quality risks before development is completed, working with the Business Analyst and Project Manager to resolve them
Design and maintain test scenarios, test cases, scripts, checklists and test-data requirements covering positive, negative, boundary, exception and end-to-end scenarios.
Link test cases to the relevant requirements, user stories or acceptance criteria to maintain traceability.
Defect Management
Log defects with clear reproduction steps, expected and actual results, evidence, environment details and business impact
Classify defects according to agreed severity and priority definitions
Facilitate defect-triage sessions with developers, business analysts, project managers, vendors and business representatives.
Track defects through investigation, resolution, retesting and closure, identifying whether defects originate within an application or at an integration boundary.
UAT Support & Release Readiness
Work with the Business Analyst, Project Manager and business stakeholders to prepare the UAT approach and business-focused UAT scenarios
Confirm UAT environment, user access and test data readiness, and brief business testers on the UAT process and defect-logging requirements
Support users during execution and help distinguish defects from requirement changes, training needs, configuration issues or enhancement requests.
Track UAT progress, defects, decisions and sign-offs, and provide evidence-based release-readiness recommendations, ensuring outstanding defects and accepted risks are communicated before business approval.
Regression Testing
Develop and maintain regression packs for business-critical applications and recurring release cycles
Identify existing functionality that may be affected by new development, configuration changes or defect corrections
Execute regression testing before significant releases and after material changes, and track regression coverage and gaps across releases.
Recommend suitable candidates for test automation based on frequency, stability, risk and repeatability.
Requirements :
Qualifications:
Diploma or degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering or a related discipline
ISTQB Foundation certification.
Experience:
5–10 years’ experience in software quality assurance, software testing, test analysis or a comparable role
Preparing test strategies, test plans, test cases, test scripts and regression packs
Testing web applications, mobile applications, enterprise systems or transactional platforms
Performing functional, system, integration, end-to-end and regression testing
Managing defects through the complete defect lifecycle
Working directly with developers, business analysts, project managers, business users and external vendors in Agile, Waterfall or hybrid environments
Producing clear testing reports and presenting quality risks to stakeholders.
Advantageous:
Experience within QSR, retail, hospitality, franchising or multi-site operations
Testing POS, voucher, loyalty, payment, ordering or other high-volume transactional systems
Testing APIs and integrated systems
Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, SharePoint and Dataverse

Be responsible for the financial hygiene of the Exports and Food Service financials.
Overseeing internal and external audits.

Budgeting and forecasting financial modelling.
Strategic business development scenario planning and modelling.

Cost management and variance reporting i.e. reviewing fixed cost spend with the Customer and Marketing Director on their respective areas, and marketing investment effectiveness tracking.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING TO THE TABLE
Key attributes and competencies
Strong financial control and governance skills, including reporting accuracy, audit oversight and risk management.
Strong financial modelling and analytical capabilities to support budgeting, forecasting and strategic scenario planning.
Commercial acumen, with the ability to evaluate pricing, revenue performance, cost drivers and marketing investment effectiveness.
Effective business partnering, presentation and influencing skills, with the confidence to constructively challenge senior stakeholders.
Ability to lead finance digital transformation, systems adoption and continuous process improvement.
Strong leadership and accountability, with the ability to manage competing priorities across stakeholders, countries and categories.
Experience
Relevant commercial finance and finance business partnering experience in FMCG, with increasing responsibility.
Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling and cost management.
Experience managing audits, financial controls and risk processes, and delivering finance improvement initiatives.
CA(SA) qualification essential.
WHAT YOU WILL BE MEASURED ON
Financial reporting accuracy and timeliness: Monthly Exports and Food Service reporting delivered to Group Finance by agreed deadlines, with minimal errors or subsequent adjustments.
Planning and forecast quality: Sales plans, budgets and forecasts approved on time, with forecast accuracy tracked against actual results and material variances clearly explained.
Financial governance and audit outcomes: Effective financial controls, timely closure of audit findings and an up-to-date risk register with agreed mitigation actions tracked to completion.
Revenue management effectiveness: Accurate and timely pricing implementation, adoption of the CAT tool and measurable contribution to margin improvement.
Cost and investment management: Timely identification of spend variances, delivery of agreed cost actions and evaluation of marketing investment effectiveness.
Commercial decision support: Timely, robust financial models and scenario analyses that inform business development and investment decisions, with reviews of outcomes against assumptions.
Finance transformation delivery: Agreed digital initiatives delivered to plan, with demonstrated adoption and measurable improvements in reporting speed, accuracy or manual effort.
Business partnering effectiveness: Weekly sales estimates completed with the Customer team, agreed actions followed through and stakeholder feedback demonstrating the value of finance support.

Job Description
Are you the kind of communicator who spots a typo from across the room, turns raw information into compelling stories, and knows how to make a brand's voice impossible to ignore?
Raizcorp is looking for a Communications Officer to join our Marketing team. This is not a "write a post and tick a box" role. We are looking for a sharp, creative, deadline-driven communicator who can write, edit, proof, interview, plan, coordinate, publish, analyse and keep multiple communication balls in the air without dropping the brand.
You will support the Marketing Manager and take responsibility for a wide range of internal and external communications, ensuring that Raizcorp and its allied companies speak with one clear, professional and powerful voice.
What you'll be doing
You will be the person who helps turn strategy into stories, ideas into campaigns, and business activity into high-quality content. Your work will include:
Writing and editing content such as thought leadership articles, video, podcast and event scripts, press releases, blog posts, newsletters, sales proposals (including brochures, manuals and more), marketing collateral, website copy and social media content.
Helping to develop and execute communication and social media strategies across different audiences and platforms.
Proofreading and quality-checking content to ensure that every piece of communication is accurate, polished and brand-aligned.
Managing and updating websites, portals and online content, including working with developers and suppliers when new digital platforms or website updates are required.
Finding newsworthy stories inside the business, interviewing entrepreneurs, gathering information, sourcing images and writing stories that bring impact to life.
Supporting events, launches and expos by capturing stories, photographs and video content where required.
Managing the organisation's central information email inbox, responding to and directing enquiries from entrepreneurs, stakeholders and prospective clients, monitoring campaign responses, newsletter enquiries and lead-generation communications, and ensuring timely, professional follow-up.
Acting as the primary liaison with Raizcorp's appointed Public Relations agency, coordinating media opportunities, press releases, approvals, campaign activities, interview requests and all related communications to ensure alignment with organisational objectives.
Liaising with PR, communications, digital, print and branding suppliers to keep projects moving and deadlines on track.
Managing external freelance writers by preparing content briefs, coordinating assignments, reviewing and editing submissions, providing feedback, monitoring deadlines and ensuring all content meets Raizcorp's editorial and brand standards.
Tracking content progress, reporting on communication activity and helping to analyse the effectiveness of external communications.
Keeping content, reports, press clippings and documentation organised, filed and easy to access.
This role is for you if…
You are a natural storyteller with the discipline of an editor.
You care deeply about accuracy, grammar, tone and detail.
You can move between a press release, a social media post, a website update, a video script, and a stakeholder email without losing focus.
You are comfortable interviewing people, asking good questions and turning conversations into meaningful content.
You thrive in a fast-paced environment where deadlines matter and priorities can shift.
You are proactive, organised and willing to roll up your sleeves to get the job done.
You are confident coordinating multiple external service providers and contributors while maintaining quality, consistency and deadlines.
You understand that great communication is not just about writing well; it is about protecting the brand, understanding the audience and delivering the right message at the right time.
What you'll need
A degree or national diploma in Journalism, Corporate Communications, Publishing, Public Relations or a related field.
At least five years' relevant experience in editing, writing, journalism or communications.
Excellent writing, editing, proofreading, research, interviewing and presentation skills.
A proven track record across a broad range of communication activities, including media, press releases, websites, publications, marketing, social media and events.
Experience creating content for websites and working with content management systems.
Experience with e-communications, including newsletters.
Experience developing or executing digital initiatives and campaigns across social media platforms.
Experience coordinating Public Relations activities and working with external PR agencies or media partners would be advantageous.
Experience managing shared communication inboxes, stakeholder correspondence and external content contributors would be advantageous.
Strong interpersonal and networking skills, with the ability to liaise professionally with internal teams, suppliers and external stakeholders.
The ability to manage projects from start to finish while keeping deadlines, details and stakeholders under control.
Intermediate MS Office skills.
An understanding of social media analytics would be advantageous.
Basic photography skills would be helpful but are not essential.

Job Description:
Role Purpose
The Mechanical Supervisor will coordinate and oversee the production, installation, testing and commissioning of mechanical and piping services at water and wastewater treatment plants, pump stations and related bulk infrastructure. The role involves working closely with engineers, the civil, electrical and instrumentation teams, suppliers and the client to make sure installations meet specifications, as well as managing site coordination, production and safety on site.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Planning and Programming
Advise on how mechanical installations should be coordinated, sequenced and resourced, in line with the civil, electrical and instrumentation works.
Interpret and check drawings, including general arrangements, process and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), pipework isometrics and supplier drawings, and identify and report any discrepancies.
Make sure discrepancies, clashes and outstanding information are identified and resolved in good time, before they affect the programme.
Plan when equipment, pipework, fittings and valves will be delivered, and check that cast-in items, plinths and holding-down bolts are ready before installation starts.
Help plan shutdowns, tie-ins and connections to existing live plant, together with the client’s operations staff.
Mechanical Installations
Supervise the installation of pumps, motors, blowers, mixers, aerators and other process equipment.
Supervise the fabrication and installation of process and bulk pipework in steel, stainless steel, ductile iron, HDPE and uPVC, including flanged, welded, butt-fused and mechanical joints.
Oversee the installation of valves and fittings, including sluice, butterfly, non-return, air and pressure-reducing valves, actuators, flow meters and surge vessels.
Coordinate the installation of treatment plant equipment such as screens, grit removal systems, clarifier and thickener mechanisms, filters, chemical dosing systems, and overhead cranes and hoists.
Make sure equipment is correctly levelled, grouted, aligned (shaft and coupling alignment), torqued and supported, including pipe supports and thrust restraints.
Coordinate and witness pressure and leak testing, flushing, disinfection, pre-commissioning, commissioning and performance testing with engineers, suppliers and the client.
Make sure mechanical equipment is received, inspected, stored and protected correctly on site.
Site Administration
Follow company policies and procedures for site management.
Monitor subcontractor and supplier progress, and make sure orders for labour, plant and materials are placed on time.
Prepare and submit daily site diaries, progress, coordination and scheduling reports.
Keep records of labour, plant and materials, and report on productivity against planned targets.
Report variations, delays and technical queries (RFIs) to the Site Agent or Project Manager early.
Quality Assurance
Implement and monitor the Project Quality Plan and inspection and test plans (ITPs) for mechanical works, making sure hold and witness points are respected.
Inspect workmanship and materials, carry out snagging, and report and follow up corrective actions for non-compliance.
Compile quality records for handover, including test certificates, pressure test records, alignment reports, operation and maintenance information, and as-built drawings.
SHEQ Assurance
Maintain site safety standards in line with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, the Construction Regulations (2014) and company requirements.
Make sure working conditions and equipment are safe, and that the correct PPE is issued and used.
Lead toolbox talks and risk assessments, and make sure permit-to-work systems are followed, particularly for confined spaces, lifting operations, hot work, working at height and isolation/lockout.
Manage the specific hazards of working on live water and wastewater sites, including hazardous gases, biological hazards and treatment chemicals.
Make sure environmental controls are in place, including spill prevention and managing bypass pumping and discharges.
People Leadership
Lead, motivate and allocate work to fitters, pipe fitters, welders, riggers, plumbers and general workers.
Train and mentor junior staff and apprentices, and promote teamwork, discipline and accountability on site.
Qualifications
Completion of N2 or N3 (NTC) trade theory.
Ideally, a completed and passed trade test (Fitter, Fitter and Turner, Millwright, Boilermaker or Plumber), as specified in the Manpower Training Act (section 28 or 13), or a relevant qualification under the Skills Development Act.
A National Diploma in Mechanical Engineering will be an advantage.
Health and safety training (e.g. SHE Representative, First Aid, Confined Space Entry) will be an advantage.
A valid driver’s licence.
Experience
At least 12 years of related experience in the construction or engineering environment, with at least 8 years supervising mechanical installations at water or wastewater treatment plants, pump stations or bulk water projects.
Hands-on experience installing, testing and commissioning pumps, pipework, valves and process equipment.
Candidates may be required to work outside the Western Cape, but their home base will ideally be in Cape Town.
Core Competencies
Technical Competencies
Mechanical installation: pump and equipment installation, alignment, pipework systems, valves, pressure testing and commissioning.
Drawing interpretation: reading and interpreting general arrangements, P&IDs, isometrics and supplier drawings.
Process understanding: a working knowledge of how water and wastewater treatment processes and pump stations work.
Industry knowledge: mechanical and piping materials, plant, tools and equipment.
Construction knowledge: construction processes and trades, and how civil, mechanical, electrical and instrumentation work fits together.
Site administration: site administration systems, reporting and construction team coordination.
Compliance: health and safety legislation, relevant SANS standards and quality management requirements.
Behavioural Competencies
Communication: strong written and spoken English.
Planning and numeracy: good with numbers and strong at planning.
Problem-solving: solves problems effectively and manages conflict well.
Drive for results: a proven track record of driving production and making firm decisions.
Leadership: excellent interpersonal skills and able to delegate effectively.
Safety commitment: leads by example and does not compromise on safety.
Teamwork: computer literate and a team player.

Support cash flow improvement through disciplined working capital management, including focused monitoring of inventory, debtors and creditors
Monitor debtor ageing with the finance department, escalate collection risks and support agreed recovery actions

Coordinate and consolidate forecasts for review and approval by the Finance Executive: Trade
Monitor and analyses financial performance against budget and forecast, highlighting variances, risks and recommended actions
Support the finance teams across the Trade division and promote consistent financial processes, controls, assumptions and reporting practices across the underlying businesses
Monitor inventory controls and working capital indicators, and recommend actions to reduce stockouts, excess stock, obsolescence and unnecessary carrying costs
Support the Trade finance teams with the implementation and monitoring of cost-control measures that improve efficiency and profitability while maintaining operational and quality requirements
Ensure consistent and accurate inventory costing across the relevant Trade businesses, including the appropriate allocation of direct costs and production overheads
Ensure the consistent and accurate costing of inventory across the relevant Trade businesses
Review the consolidated monthly financial statements, management reports and supporting analyses for the Trade division, and provide clear insight into financial performance, trends, risks and opportunities

Coordinate the identification, monitoring and escalation of material financial, control, tax and compliance risks across the Trade division. Support the implementation of agreed remedial actions and provide the Finance Executive: Trade with consolidated visibility of significant exposures, overdue actions and recurring control weaknesses
Continuously improve the integrity, accuracy, relevance and timeliness of financial reporting, and escalate significant matters to the Finance Executive: Trade
Support the Finance Executive: Trade and Group Insurance in maintaining adequate insurance cover for divisional assets and ensuring that relevant asset information is complete and current
Work closely with the Finance Executive: Trade, Trade Financial Managers, Group Finance and other internal departments to streamline financial processes, improve information flow and support consistent reporting requirements
Provide additional financial reporting, analysis and related support as reasonably required by the Finance Executive: Trade or senior management

Founded in 1953 on a farm in the Randburg district, the College today is encircled by the northern suburbs of Johannesburg. Established as a boys’ school, the College took the bold step to build a girls’ school on the campus in 1995, creating the possibility of a unique synergy model.

St Stithi...read moreans is a Methodist School and a circuit of the Central District of the Methodist Church of Southern Africa. The College subscribes to a Statement of Spirituality that outlines our core beliefs and values.

Students enter the College through the gateway of the Junior Prep on the lower campus, a co-educational school of 480 girls and boys in Grades R to 2. From Grade 3 onwards, the boys and girls move into separate Preparatory Schools of 400 students each.

A second "gateway" into St Stithians is offered to entrants of Grade 8 as they embark on their high school journey in the Boys’ College of 780 students and the Girls’ College of 530 students.

A number of benchmarks, both national and international, provide a framework for evaluating quality.

Grade 12 students write the matriculation examinations of the Independent Examinations Board (IEB). Our matriculants achieve at a high level, with 96-98% obtaining Bachelor degree passes for entry to South African universities and universities in Europe, North America and Australia. View our latest Matric results here.

Our campus is a place of natural beauty, with various landscape zones, and the College is committed to being an environmentally "green" school.

Our students matriculate as well-rounded individuals, well prepared to inspire excellence and make a difference both in our own country, the African continent and globally.

Job Description:
Key Accountabilities and Outputs:
Electrical Safety and Compliance
Apply lockout, tagout, test-for-dead and permit-to-work requirements before starting electrical work.
Inspect the work area, identify hazards and use the prescribed personal protective equipment and test instruments.
Stop and report unsafe equipment, damaged protection devices, exposed conductors, bypassed interlocks and other immediate risks.
Maintain panel access, covers, labels, earthing, guarding and electrical housekeeping to the required standard.
Complete statutory and internal electrical inspections assigned to the role and record all defects and corrective actions.
Follow site emergency, fire prevention, environmental and incident-reporting procedures.
Planned and Preventive Maintenance
Complete scheduled electrical maintenance on textile production machinery, motors, drives, control panels, conveyors, pumps, fans, compressors, heating systems, utility equipment and building services.
Inspect and test cables, terminations, contactors, overloads, isolators, protective devices, sensors, switches, solenoids, power supplies and control circuits.
Identify developing defects such as overheating, loose connections, insulation damage, nuisance tripping, abnormal current draw and deteriorating components.
Plan work with the Electrical Foreman and production teams so that maintenance is completed during agreed stoppages and shutdowns.
Record findings, parts used, labour time, follow-up work and equipment condition in the maintenance management system.
Breakdown Response and Fault Finding
Respond promptly to electrical breakdowns and obtain clear information about the fault, operating conditions and production impact.
Use electrical drawings, test equipment, alarms, drive diagnostics and programmable logic controller input and output status to locate faults systematically.
Repair or replace defective components, complete functional and safety tests, and confirm that the equipment is safe before handover to production.
Escalate complex control, automation or instrumentation faults to the appropriate specialist and provide accurate diagnostic information.
Investigate recurring failures, identify the underlying cause and implement or recommend corrective action rather than relying on temporary repairs.
Communicate progress, expected restoration time, residual risk and follow-up work to the Electrical Foreman and affected production personnel.
Electrical Installations and Improvements
Install and modify motors, isolators, distribution equipment, cable routes, control panels, lighting, field devices and associated wiring in accordance with approved drawings and specifications.
Support the testing and commissioning of new or modified equipment, including rotation checks, protection checks, interlock tests and safe start-up.
Do not make unauthorized changes to programmable logic controller programs, safety circuits, protection settings or machine interlocks.
Mark up drawings and provide accurate information for updates to schematics, cable schedules, equipment registers and maintenance plans.
Identify practical opportunities to improve reliability, energy use, maintainability and electrical safety, and submit recommendations through the agreed change-control process.
Maintenance Control and Resources
Create, update and close work orders with a clear description of the fault, action taken, parts used and further work required.
Check critical electrical spares and advise the Electrical Foreman when stock levels, obsolescence or lead times could create operational risk.
Keep tools, meters, test leads, ladders and portable equipment secure, serviceable and within required calibration or inspection dates.
Maintain a clean work area and remove waste, redundant cables, packaging and replaced components after every task.
Participate in maintenance planning, shift handovers, toolbox talks, risk assessments and post-breakdown reviews.
Teamwork and Technical Support
Work constructively with production operators, artisans, technicians, contractors and engineers to diagnose and resolve equipment problems.
Give clear shift handovers covering outstanding defects, isolated equipment, temporary controls, parts required and work still in progress.
Provide task guidance to electrical assistants and apprentices within the limits of competence and delegated authority.
Monitor contractors working on assigned electrical tasks and immediately report unsafe work, poor workmanship or deviation from scope.
Share technical knowledge and lessons from failures to improve team capability and prevent recurrence.
Requirements
Matric with Maths/Maths lit
Recognized Electrician Trade Test certificate
Five to ten years of post-trade industrial electrical maintenance experience in a manufacturing or process environment
Practical experience with three-phase systems, motors, motor control, switchgear, variable speed drives, control circuits and industrial distribution
Ability to diagnose electrical and control faults methodically using drawings, meters, alarms and equipment diagnostics
Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, single-line diagrams, panel layouts, manuals and equipment specifications
Working knowledge of maintenance management systems, electronic work orders and standard office software
Willingness to work shifts, standby, call outs, weekends and planned shutdowns when rostered

Job Description:
MRM Revenue and Reconciliation is part of the De Beers Mining and Discovery (M&D) Mineral Resource Management (MRM) technical team and encompasses Diamond Revenue Analysis (DRA) and diamond revenue modelling for both operations and projects. The department is responsible for creating and maintaining revenue models for all De Beers group mines and creating revenue estimates for potential new mines based on sample data. It generates the revenue estimates and forecasts which are the primary source of price information used for financial management models, the Life of Asset Business Plans, Resource and Reserve statements and the DBGSS Intentions to Offer (ITOs). The department also provides technical and strategic leadership to revenue contacts throughout the De Beers Group.
The purpose of this role is to act as the Group’s subject matter expert and owner for revenue estimation and forecasting within De Beers. It ensures that Diamond Revenue models are developed to an appropriate level of confidence, providing reliable inputs to support operational and strategic decision making across the Group.
Key Tasks:
Define and implement Diamond Resource Revenue Models for all De Beers Group operations, and potential future mines based on sample data.
Ensure Diamond Revenue Modelling and Diamond Revenue Analysis (DRA) within the Group, comply with business requirements, reporting codes and regulations prevailing in the country of activities.
Define Diamond Revenue Modelling processes and guidelines from sampling through to forecasting, and their practical application into M&D MRM and the Business Units (BU’s).
Uphold strong diamond data validation processes and guidelines to ensure revenue and assortment inputs are accurate, statistically robust and fit for purpose.
Ensure Diamond Revenue Models are aligned to the latest De Beers Group Price Book, ensuring alignment across operations and clear reconciliation of resulting Price Book changes.
Compile Revenue Forecasts for the BU’s, Group Finance and GSS based on operational plans and budgets from Business Planning submissions (data calls).
Reconcile revenue estimates and forecasts per series per unit, identifying assortment variances and clearly defining the impact on operational revenues, processing plans and GSS supply.
Develop and maintain appropriate Mineral Resource Classification Scorecards for Revenue within the Mineral Resource Classification System ensuring appropriate confidence rating of resources and reserves in line with applicable reporting codes (e.g. SAMREC).
Develop and maintain a technical risk register for Diamond Revenue management, as part of the Resource and Reserve Risk register, highlighting areas of concern to be addressed by the operational teams.
Deconvolute revenue data where production is combined ensuring revenues are appropriately allocated to the affected operations.
Act as the primary interface with Competent Persons, Group Sightholder Sales, Pricing & Development, reporting and Group Strategy on Diamond Resource Revenue matters.
Promotion of all aspects of SHE.
Support broader Mineral Resource Management governance across the Group
Contribute to functional reviews of resource models to ensure revenue is appropriately represented
Drive improved business performance through the effective application of Diamond Revenue expertise
Develop and support talent within Diamond Revenue modelling and reconciliation.
Align and strengthen discipline health, including standards, practices and technical development across the Group.
Qualifications:
Tertiary qualification in a mining discipline, geosciences, statistics, econometrics or similar.
Registered professional and full member of relevant professional discipline institute (Preferred)
Experience statement should include reference to:
5 years’ experience at a senior level (Mining discipline, diamond sorting & sales, diamond pricing).
Experience defining standards, guidelines, and processes
Experience identifying and mitigating Operational risks
Experience in the evaluation of projects & operations.
Knowledge and Skills
Technical:
Advanced understanding of the entire diamond pipeline including sorting and aggregation and sales.
Experience with mining governance, audit processes, and reporting systems
Understanding of Diamond Revenue Analysis
Expert understanding of the GSS diamond assortment and Group sales strategy.

Job Description:
We are seeking an Insurance Manager to act as De Beers Group’s central authority on insurance and risk financing. The role will manage global insurance programmes across mining operations, diamond recovery and processing, global diamond transportation, inventory/specie exposures, retail businesses, corporate functions and strategic initiatives, with accountability for effective risk transfer, claims recovery, regulatory compliance, loss prevention and optimisation of the Group’s total cost of risk.
The role has global scope and requires travel to corporate and operational locations, including mining sites, as business needs require. The role holder will coordinate business-unit insurance representatives and external service providers; any direct-report responsibilities and delegated financial authorities as defined.
Key Responsibilities
Insurance Strategy and Programme Design
Develop and implement the Group's global insurance strategy and risk financing framework.
Define the Group’s risk appetite for insured and retained risks and recommend appropriate deductibles, self-insured retentions, limits, insurer panels and alternative risk financing arrangements.
Design, procure and maintain appropriate insurance programmes to meet the evolving needs of the business, including:
Mining and operational assets
Capital projects and construction activities
Mergers and acquisitions
Corporate and commercial activities
Emerging and strategic risks
Maintain a coverage framework addressing material exposures, including property damage and business interruption, construction, liability, marine cargo/specie, cyber, directors’ and officers’ liability, crime, environmental liability, political violence and terrorism, and other specialist risks relevant to the Group.
Ensure all statutory, contractual and regulatory insurance requirements are met across jurisdictions in which De Beers operates.
Lead insurance market engagements, renewals and placement activities to secure optimal coverage and competitive pricing.
Monitor global insurance market trends, capacity, pricing and coverage developments to identify opportunities and emerging threats.
Provide insurance due diligence and transaction support for acquisitions, divestments, restructurings, joint ventures and strategic projects.
Establish insurance governance for non- government joint ventures and partnerships, including alignment with partners, financing requirements and shareholder obligations.
Build and maintain institutional insurance knowledge within the Group and develop sustainable insurance management processes that reduce reliance on external advisers.
Programme Optimisation and Innovation
Continuously review insurance arrangements to identify cost-effective improvements and innovative risk financing solutions.
Challenge existing programme structures and develop recommendations that improve coverage, reduce total cost of risk and increase operational efficiency.
Explore alternative risk transfer mechanisms and emerging insurance products.
Benchmark insurance programmes against industry best practice and leading mining sector standards.
Insurance Administration and Governance
Oversee the implementation and ongoing management of all administrative processes and controls necessary for the effective operation of insurance programmes.
Ensure accurate and timely management of policy documentation, endorsements, declarations, asset schedules and underwriting data.
Establish and maintain governance frameworks, reporting mechanisms and internal controls supporting insurance programme effectiveness.
Own insurance the budgets, premium forecasts, allocations and accruals; monitor broker remuneration, premium taxes and expenditure against approved budgets.
Coordinate with Finance, Tax and external audit on insurance-related accounting, claims receivables, provisions, disclosures and supporting evidence.
Maintain compliance with local admitted-policy requirements, licensing, sanctions, anti-bribery, premium-tax, data-protection and document-retention obligations across relevant jurisdictions.
Own insurance exposure, policy and claims data, systems and records, including data-quality controls, access governance and reporting automation.
Coordinate annual renewal processes and ensure quality submission information is provided to insurers and brokers.
Claims Management
Lead the Group response to major loss events and significant or complex claims, coordinating insurers, brokers, loss adjusters, legal advisers and operational stakeholders to maximise recovery, protect evidence and minimise business disruption.
Develop and maintain effective claims management processes across the Group.
Ensure appropriate claims notification, documentation and recovery procedures are in place and operating effectively.
Monitor claims performance metrics and ensure claims are settled within reasonable timeframes and in accordance with policy terms and conditions.
Identify trends and lessons learned from claims experience and recommend risk mitigation measures.
Stakeholder Management and Advisory
Establish and coordinate a network of insurance coordinators and subject matter experts across operations, projects, finance, legal, security, supply chain and procurement functions to ensure accurate underwriting and claims information is available throughout the year.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with business unit leaders, project teams and Group functions.
Provide expert insurance advice and support to operational, project and corporate teams.
Review insurance, indemnity, limitation-of-liability, waiver and evidence-of-insurance provisions in material customer, supplier, logistics, construction, financing and joint-venture agreements.
Maintain relationships with insurers, brokers, reinsurers, loss adjusters, legal advisors and other external stakeholders.
Act as the owner of the broker relationship and provide independent challenge to broker recommendations, programme structure, insurer selection, coverage terms and placement strategies.
Stay informed on business developments, strategic initiatives and risk exposures to proactively advise on insurance implications.
Communicate insurance requirements, programme performance and key developments to senior management.
Work with crisis management, business continuity, disaster recovery, security and operational teams to ensure insurance arrangements and incident-response protocols are aligned.
Captive Insurance Strategy
Investigate the feasibility, benefits and business case for establishing a Group captive insurance company.
Assess captive structures, domiciles, governance requirements and financial implications.
Lead implementation activities should the Group decide to establish a captive insurance vehicle.
Manage ongoing interactions with captive managers, regulators, actuaries and reinsurers where applicable.
Reporting and Risk Management
Prepare and present insurance and claims reports for senior management, executive committees and governance forums.
Monitor total cost of risk, insurance spend and claims recovery performance.
Support enterprise risk management processes by providing insurance expertise and risk financing insights.
Develop and maintain insurance-related key performance indicators (KPIs) and management information.
Track and report performance against agreed measures, including renewal delivery, premium versus budget, claims recovery and ageing, uninsured exposures, closure of risk-engineering actions and stakeholder service levels.

Deliver insurance separation readiness, including transfer or replacement of policies, data, systems and services; define transitional service requirements; and confirm responsibility for legacy and stranded liabilities.
During the first 12 months, complete the global renewal, establish the target governance and reporting model, improve claims oversight, implement priority loss-prevention actions and deliver the captive feasibility assessment and recommendation.

The Western Cape Blood Service was established in October 1938 when the first meeting of the Cape Peninsula Blood Transfusion Service took place at Groote Schuur Hospital. It was a slow start, with only 200 donors enrolling in the first three months and an average of 30 transfusions per month.

In...read morethe 1930s, transfusion practice was in its most basic phase of development. Hospitals would request a donation and when a suitable donor was found, they would report to the hospital. There, blood would be transfused directly from the donor to the recipient with only a screen separating them – a far cry from today’s procedures!

The Service was able to provide blood serum and whole blood to military hospitals for the duration of the Second World War from 1939.

In 1942, the Service obtained its own building in St. George’s Street where three donors could be accommodated at a time. Back then, blood was collected in Horlicks milk bottles.

Job Description:
R30,000 - R35,000
About Job Role
The Commercial & Marketing Manager is a senior management position responsible for strengthening company’s commercial position, market presence, community relevance and long-term sustainability.
The role requires a commercially minded, strategic and entrepreneurial individual who understands business, media and people, and who can translate the vision and mission of the company into practical opportunities, campaigns, projects, partnerships and initiatives.
The Commercial & Marketing Manager is expected to see opportunities, develop ideas, make plans and mobilise people to turn those ideas into reality. This includes growing existing commercial initiatives, creating new concepts, building mutually beneficial relationships with businesses and organisations, and finding ways to place the company more firmly in the community and in the public conversation.
The role extends beyond traditional marketing, advertising or fundraising. It focuses on creating value and growth across the organisation through commercial projects, strategic partnerships, campaigns, events, audience engagement and community initiatives.
The Commercial & Marketing Manager forms part of the management team and works closely with the Station Manager/Content Manager, Integrated Marketing Specialist and Development & Partnership Manager, as well as other relevant teams.
The role requires an integrated approach in which content, programming, marketing, commercial development, fundraising, partnerships, events and community engagement support and strengthen one another.
This is not a siloed role. The successful candidate must be able to connect people, ideas, departments and opportunities, mobilise the appropriate teams and drive initiatives through to implementation.
The ultimate objective is to help the company to grow, become more visible and relevant, strengthen its commercial sustainability and become a station that is seen, heard, experienced, and talked about.
Key Responsibilities
Commercial Strategy & Business Development
Drive commercial growth strategies that support the long-term sustainability of the company.
Work collaboratively with the Development & Partnership Manager on commercial and income-generating opportunities, ensuring that the respective roles complement one another.
Understand the needs of businesses and organisations and create mutually beneficial opportunities connecting them with the company’s audience, platforms and community.
Create commercial concepts, proposals and packages incorporating radio, digital, events, activations and other station assets.
Build and maintain relationships with prospective clients, partners and stakeholders.
Negotiate and facilitate commercial arrangements and strategic collaborations within approved parameters.
Monitor relevant business, media and market trends and identify opportunities for growth.
Strategic Campaigns & Commercial Projects
Take overall commercial responsibility for the company’s existing income-generating projects and initiatives, ensuring that they are effectively managed, strengthened and grown.
Drive the further development and scaling of established projects and other commercial initiatives of the station.
Turn ideas and opportunities into commercially viable campaigns, projects and initiatives.
Lead projects from concept and planning through to implementation, completion and evaluation.
Look for ways to increase the commercial return, reach, participation and long-term potential of existing projects.
Bring the appropriate internal teams and external partners together to make projects happen.
Evaluate successful initiatives and explore opportunities to repeat, expand or scale them.
Business Relationships, Networking & Partnerships
Build strong relationships with business owners, executives, entrepreneurs, community leaders, and strategic stakeholders.
Maintain an active business and community network that can support future opportunities.
Represent the company at relevant networking events, business forums, conferences, and community engagements.
Create opportunities for collaboration rather than simply selling advertising or requesting sponsorship.
Develop mutually beneficial partnerships, joint campaigns, events, promotions, and community initiatives.
Maintain and grow relationships with existing commercial partners.
Represent the company professionally and act as an ambassador for its vision, mission and brand.
Market Presence, Marketing & Audience Growth
Strengthen the company’s visibility, relevance and presence within the community and broader market.
Work closely with the Station Manager/Content Manager and Integrated Marketing Specialist to align content, marketing, campaigns, promotions and commercial initiatives.
Drive initiatives that increase awareness, listenership, audience engagement and interaction with the station beyond the traditional broadcast platform.
Ensure that the company brand is consistently positioned across commercial, community, marketing and promotional activities.
Leverage radio, digital, social media, events and community platforms to create greater reach, engagement and commercial value.
Position the company as an active and relevant participant in the community – seen, heard, experienced and talked about.
Integrated Management & Leadership
Serve as a member of the company management team and contribute to the overall strategic direction of the organisation.
Work closely with the Station Manager/Content Manager, Integrated Marketing Specialist and Development & Partnership Manager to ensure that the different areas of the organisation work towards common objectives.
Ensure that commercial, marketing, content, programming, fundraising, partnership, event and community initiatives are considered from a whole-station perspective.
Bring the appropriate people together around projects and ensure that responsibilities, objectives and timelines are clearly understood.
Mobilise internal teams around strategic campaigns, projects and opportunities.
Facilitate collaboration and communication between different functional areas.
Encourage a culture of initiative, creativity, accountability and shared responsibility for the growth of the company.
Participate actively in strategic planning, brainstorming and management discussions.
Innovation & Commercialization
Look for new ideas, trends, platforms, events, partnerships and business models that could benefit the company.
Explore opportunities to use the station’s existing assets — including its on-air platforms, digital channels, events, presenters, audience and community presence — to create greater commercial value.
Develop innovative packages and concepts that combine different station assets for commercial and strategic benefit.
Encourage innovative thinking and an opportunity-driven culture across the organisation.
Assess new ideas from both a commercial and strategic perspective and, where appropriate, turn them into practical projects.
Strategic Planning & Performance
Contribute to organisational strategy, business planning and management decision-making.
Work with other members of management to establish relevant goals and KPIs.
Prepare commercial proposals, budgets, forecasts and performance reports where required.
Monitor the financial and strategic performance of projects and initiatives.
Analyse project and campaign results and recommend improvements or further opportunities.
Monitor budgets and expenses relating to projects under the employee’s responsibility.
Provide management with regular reports on commercial opportunities, projects, partnerships and performance.
KEY PERFORMANCE AREAS (KPAs)
The performance of the Commercial & Marketing Manager will be evaluated against, amongst others:
Growth in commercial revenue and new income opportunities.
Successful management, growth and scaling of existing commercial projects.
Successful development and implementation of commercial campaigns and initiatives.
Acquisition and development of strategic business relationships and partnerships.
Growth in the company’s visibility and presence within the community.
Growth in business and stakeholder engagement.
Audience growth and engagement resulting from strategic initiatives.
Successful commercialisation of station assets and platforms.
Effective collaboration and mobilisation of internal teams.
Successful integration of commercial, marketing, content, fundraising and community initiatives.
Contribution to the long-term sustainability and growth of the station.
Achievement of agreed commercial and strategic targets.
CANDIDATE REQUIREMENTS
Qualifications | Years of Experience
Relevant qualification in business management, marketing, commerce, communications, media, business development or a related field advantageous.
Proven experience in business development, commercial management, marketing, media, partnerships, sales, entrepreneurship or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to manage commercial opportunities and projects.
Experience in developing campaigns, projects, partnerships or business initiatives.
Experience dealing with business owners, executives, clients and senior stakeholders.
Experience in project management from concept through to completion.
Experience in developing presentations, proposals or commercial concepts.
Experience within the media, NPO, Christian, community or related environment is advantageous.
Strong understanding of business and commercial principles.
Skills and Competencies
Commercially minded and entrepreneurial
Strong business acumen.
Ability to speak Afrikaans and English
Strategic thinking and planning.
Ability to see the bigger picture and recognise opportunities.
Excellent relationship-building and networking skills.
Strong negotiation and deal-making ability.
Creative and innovative thinking.
Strong project and campaign management skills.
Ability to turn ideas into practical plans and measurable outcomes.
Strong leadership and team mobilisation skills.
Excellent communication and presentation skills.
Ability to influence and inspire others.
Strong initiative and self-motivation.
Financial and commercial awareness.
Ability to work across different functions and bring people together.
Strong organisational and problem-solving skills.
Other Requirements
Values, Mission & Cultural Fit
The Commercial & Marketing Manager must demonstrate a genuine alignment with the Christian values, vision and mission of the company.
The successful candidate must be able to represent the company with integrity, professionalism and credibility in both the Christian community and the broader business and commercial environment.
The role requires an individual who is passionate about people, business, media, community and creating positive impact, and who is able to combine commercial thinking with the values and purpose of a Christian media organisation.
The successful candidate must be comfortable working in a collaborative environment where the success of the organisation as a whole takes precedence over individual departmental interests.
General Responsibilities
Uphold the values, vision and mission of the company at all times.
Maintain professionalism, confidentiality and integrity in all stakeholder interactions.
Represent the company positively and professionally in the business and community environment.
Work collaboratively with internal teams and external stakeholders.
Take responsibility for agreed projects, initiatives and outcomes.
Maintain professional relationships with clients, partners, suppliers and other stakeholders.
Ensure that projects and initiatives are conducted professionally and in accordance with approved budgets and organisational requirements.
Perform additional duties reasonably related to the role as required by management from time to time.

Summary:
To facilitate the risk management process by assisting the organisation to identify, analyse risk and maintain risk register, as well as developing and implementing enterprise -wide risk and treasury risk reduction programs aimed at enhancing the long term and efficiency to ensure that the company is at the forefront of managing and reporting on its risk and that its operations are conducted within best practise, corporate governance and cost management principles.

B Degree Economics or Commerce

Risk Governance

Risk Identification
Continuously identify enterprise -wide risk exposures
Assess risk rating against control adequacy.
Ensure that all projects’ risk exposure is identified, quantified, documented, and communicated.
Adopt a proactive approach in recommending and utilising international best practice.

Research, evaluate and recommend risk management and mitigation steps.
Facilitate divisional integration where risk exposures and mitigation responsibility overlap between divisions.

Evaluate the risk assessment performed by Risk Owners within the Divisions to ensure that these are an accurate representation of the risk profile of the Division.
Identify and analyse the correlation between risk drivers and control failures.
Develop and maintain enterprise-wide risk profile. Monitoring of key risk indicators and reporting against risk appetite and tolerance thresholds.

Test Compliance against Risk Policy
Challenge the mitigation or control measures applied by the Division or Department in mitigation risks where necessary.
Ensure that risk mitigation actions are timeously implemented, and non-conformances are reported to the Risk Manager and Chief Risk Officer,
Develop a risk awareness culture.
Contribute to the Combined Assurance Initiative to enhance internal control environment.
Reporting
Develop, maintain, and regularly update Divisional and Departmental risk registers.
Prepare Risk Assessment Reports for Divisions.
Provide risk dashboards to the Risk Manager and Chief Risk Officer highlighting key risk issues and mitigation measures.
Provide timeous and accurate input to the risk management reports to the Risk Manager and Chief Risk Officer

Job Title: Food and Beverage Service Expert(Waiter) - The Cape Town Edition (Pre-opening)
Job Description:
POSITION SUMMARY
Our jobs aren’t just about putting food on the table that our guests will enjoy until they ask for their bill. Instead, we want to build an experience that is memorable and unique – with food and drinks on the side. Our F&B Service Experts take the initiative and deliver a wide range of services to make sure that guests enjoy their meal. Whether setting tables, communicating with the kitchen, interacting and serving guests, or cleaning work areas and supplies, the F&B Service Expert makes transactions feel like part of the experience.
No matter what position you are in, there are a few things that are critical to success – creating a safe workplace, following company policies and procedures, upholding quality standards, and ensuring your uniform, personal appearance, and communications are professional. Doing all these things well (and other reasonable job duties as requested) is critical for F&B Service Experts – to get it right for our guests and our business each and every time.
CRITICAL TASKS
Guest Relations
Address guests' service needs in a professional, positive, and timely manner.
Welcome and acknowledge each and every guest with a smile, eye contact, and a friendly verbal greeting, using the guest's name when possible.
Anticipate guests' service needs, including asking questions of guests to better understand their needs and watching/listening to guest preferences and acting on them whenever possible.
Thank guests with genuine appreciation and provide a fond farewell.
Actively listen and respond positively to guest questions, concerns, and requests using brand or property specific process (enter brand specific programs) to resolve issues, delight, and build trust.
Engage guests in conversation regarding their stay, property services, and area attractions/offerings.
Assist other employees to ensure proper coverage and prompt guest service.
General Food and Beverage Services
Maintain cleanliness of work and guest areas by clearing, collecting and returning food and beverage items to proper area.
Maintain cleanliness of work areas throughout the day, practicing clean-as-you-go procedures.
Communicate additional meal requirements, allergies, dietary needs, and special requests to the kitchen.
Set tables according to type of event and service standards, including types of linens, glassware, plate/chinaware, and silver/flatware, ensuring all supplies meet quality standards.
Pick-up trays and clean tables as needed to ensure a clean dining area.
Follow appropriate procedures for serving alcohol, follow local Training & Guidance.
Thank every guest upon departure, invites them to return, and wishes them a fond farewell.
Retrieve and deliver food and beverage orders in a timely manner.
Perform other reasonable duties as requested.
Coordinates with the respective kitchens to ensure guests’ orders are delivered.

Follow property control audit standards and cash handling procedures (e.g., blind drops).
Count bank at end of shift, complete designated cashier reports, resolve any discrepancies, drop off receipts, and secure bank.

Transport bank to/from assigned workstation, following security procedures.
Set up and organize cashier workstation with designated supplies, forms, and resource materials; and always maintain cleanliness of workstation.
Closing
Complete closing duties, including storing all reusable goods, breaking down goods, cleaning all equipment and areas, returning equipment to proper locations, locking refrigerators, restocking items, turning off lights, locking doors, and completing daily cleaning checklist.
Steps of Service
Present physical and accurate check and process payment, adhering to all cash handling and credit policies/procedures including added and received gratuity.
Check in with guests to ensure satisfaction with each food course and/or beverages.
Answer questions on menu selections, and check with kitchen staff whenever additional clarification is necessary.
Communicate with the kitchen regarding the length of wait for food items, recook orders, and product availability.

Take room service orders over the phone, answering any questions regarding the menu, inputting order into appropriate system, up-selling, following method of payment policies, reading back the order to confirm its accuracy, and providing expected delivery time.
Place and log call back for room service order within appropriate time frame to ensure guest satisfaction.
Notify guests and management of delays in service delivery.

Communicate with guests, other employees, or departments to ensure guest needs are met.
Communication
Speak to guests and co-workers using clear, appropriate and professional language.
Discuss work topics, activities, or problems with coworkers, supervisors, or managers discreetly and quietly, avoiding public areas of the property.

Complete appropriate safety training and certifications to perform work tasks.

Follow company and department policies and procedures.
Ensure uniform, nametags, and personal appearance are clean, hygienic, professional and in compliance with company policies and procedures.

Follow the requirements and tasks as defined in EMEA Food & Beverage Cashiering SOP if associate handles cash.

Job Description:
Position Summary
Marriott International is seeking a dynamic, commercially focused, and inspirational General Manager to lead Protea Hotel Fire & Ice! Cape Town, one of Cape Town's most vibrant lifestyle hospitality destinations.
The General Manager will be responsible for the overall leadership, strategic direction, operational performance, guest satisfaction, financial results, and talent development of the hotel. This role requires a highly visible leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment, has a passion for creating memorable guest experiences, and possesses the commercial acumen to drive sustainable business success.
The successful candidate will have a proven track record of leading high-performing teams, delivering strong financial performance, and fostering a culture of service excellence.
Required Qualifications
Minimum 2-5 years of General Manager experience within a full-service hotel environment.
Demonstrated success in driving strong commercial and operational results.
Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong financial acumen and understanding of hotel performance metrics.
Proven ability to lead, motivate, and develop diverse teams.
Experience within Food & Beverage-led or lifestyle hospitality environments is highly desirable.
JOB SPECIFIC TASKS
Business Strategy Development

Job Title: Engineering Supervisor - Protea Hotel Fire & Ice! by Marriott® Johannesburg Melrose Arch
Job Description:
POSITION SUMMARY
Install, maintain, perform preventative maintenance on, and recommend replacement of tools, appliances, and equipment. Job Title: Concierge - The Cape Town Edition Hotel (Pre-opening)
Job Description:
POSITION SUMMARY
Respond to guest requests for special arrangements or services (e.g., transportation, reservations, dry cleaning) by making arrangements or identifying appropriate providers. Respond to special requests from guests with unique needs and follow up to ensure satisfaction. Gather, summarize, and provide information to guests about the property and the surrounding area amenities, including special events and activities. Answer, record, and process all guest calls, messages, requests, questions, or concerns. Contact appropriate individual or department (e.g., Bellperson, Housekeeping) as necessary to resolve guest call, request, or problem. Review shift logs/daily memo books and document pertinent information in logbooks. Monitor club lounge for seating availability, service, safety, and well-being of guests.
Report accidents, injuries, and unsafe work conditions to manager; and complete safety training and certifications. Follow all company policies and procedures, ensure uniform and personal appearance are clean and professional, maintain confidentiality of proprietary information, and protect company assets. Welcome and acknowledge all guests according to company standards, anticipate and address guests’ service needs, assist individuals with disabilities, and thank guests with genuine appreciation. Speak with others using clear and professional language, prepare and review written documents accurately and completely, and answer telephones using appropriate etiquette. Develop and maintain positive working relationships with others, support team to reach common goals, and listen and respond appropriately to the concerns of other employees. Comply with quality assurance expectations and standards. Stand, sit, or walk for an extended period of time or for an entire work shift. Company Details:
Rand Water previously known as the Rand Water Board is a South African water utility that supplies potable water to the Gauteng province and other areas of the country and is the largest water utility in Africa. The water is drawn from numerous sources and is purified and supplied to industry, minin...read moreg and local municipalities and is also involved in sanitation of waste water.

After the peace agreement between the British Government and the Boer Republics on 31 May 1902, the British, who gained control of Johannesburg realised that it was imperative to investigate the water supply and sanitation services.

On 8 May 1903 The Rand Water Board was officially established by the Rand Water Board Incorporation Ordinance No. 32 of May 1903 to supply water to the entire area.

The Rand Water Board was to include members of the Johannesburg Town Council, The Chamber of Mines, and other existing local authorities in the Witwatersrand.

In 1904 Rand Water was required to take over the undertakings of the companies at that time supplying or potentially capable of supplying water to the Witwatersrand.

Rand Water was to supply water in bulk only.
 
Water Supply 1905
It was only in 1905 that Rand Water commenced with full operations.
By 1906 the annual daily consumption of water supplied by Rand Water was about 11 Ml/d and it has been growing ever since.
In fact Rand Water’s major challenge to date has been to augment its water sources to meet the growing demand.

Job Description
The Data Engineer supports the Internal Audit function by providing independent assurance over the organisation's data landscape, including data infrastructure, data pipelines, data platforms, data quality controls, and data governance processes. The role focuses on assessing whether data is complete, accurate, reliable, secure, and appropriately governed as it moves across source systems, transformation layers, data warehouses, and reporting environments.
The Data Engineer combines strong technical data engineering expertise with an assurance mindset to evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of controls across the data lifecycle. This includes reviewing data pipelines, ETL/ELT processes, infrastructure configurations, transformation logic, reconciliation controls, and data quality monitoring processes to provide assurance over critical business and reporting data.
The role works closely with Internal Auditors, Data Engineering teams, Data Governance teams, IT, and business stakeholders to strengthen trust in organisational data and support the Internal Audit function's data-driven assurance strategy.
The Data Engineer Auditor will also where required support the Internal Audit function by applying data analytics, automation, and data‑driven techniques to enhance audit coverage, efficiency, and assurance quality.
Key Responsibilities
Data Infrastructure Assurance
Provide independent assurance over the design, implementation, security, resilience, and availability of data platforms and infrastructure.
Evaluate controls relating to cloud and on-premise data environments, including monitoring, deployment, change management, backup, and recovery processes.
Data Pipeline & Data Integrity Assurance
Assess end-to-end data flows, pipelines, and transformation processes to ensure the completeness, accuracy, integrity, and traceability of data.
Evaluate data movement, reconciliation, and lineage controls across source systems, data platforms, and reporting environments.
Data Quality & Governance
Review the effectiveness of data quality controls, governance frameworks, standards, and ownership structures.
Assess compliance with internal policies, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices relating to data management.
Data & Reporting Assurance
Evaluate data models, business rules, and reporting datasets to ensure information used for operational, financial, regulatory, and analytical decision-making is reliable and fit for purpose.
Validate the integrity of critical management and reporting information.
Audit Innovation & Continuous Assurance
Develop and maintain automated audit testing, continuous auditing capabilities, and data-driven assurance solutions.
Support Internal Audit's adoption of modern data engineering, analytics, and assurance techniques.
Data Engineering Standards & Advisory
Contribute to the development of data engineering standards, frameworks, and best practices aligned with the OUTsurance Data Strategy.
Provide assurance-related guidance to data and analytics teams on data quality, infrastructure, pipeline design, and governance practices.
Role Impact
The Data Engineer enables Internal Audit to:
Provide assurance over critical data platforms and infrastructure.
Assess the completeness and accuracy of data used for financial, operational, and regulatory reporting.
Enhance confidence in organisational data assets.
Identify risks within data pipelines and transformation processes before they impact business decisions.
Support continuous auditing and data-driven assurance.
Promote adoption of data engineering best practices aligned to the OUTsurance data strategy.
Strengthen governance, quality, and trust across the Group's data ecosystem.
Qualifications
Academic Qualifications
3-5 years' experience in Data Engineering, Data Platform Engineering, Data Architecture, or related fields.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field
Advanced SQL skills.
Strong understanding of data engineering principles and architecture.
Experience designing and reviewing data pipelines and data platforms.
Experience with data warehousing and dimensional modelling.
Strong understanding of data quality management and data governance.
Experience with cloud-native data technologies.
Understanding of DevOps, infrastructure automation, and monitoring practices.
Ability to independently assess data controls and identify risks impacting data integrity and reliability.
Technical & Analytical Skills
Understanding and knowledge of key technologies:
Cloud solutions (Databricks, Airflow, Azure, Cosmos DB)
Synapse/ Solid
SQL
PowerBI
Experience with Data Governance.
Communication & Professional Skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly explain what is relevant and important to audit stakeholders.
Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities.
High levels of drive and motivation, with a proactive approach to continuous improvement.
Creativity and innovation in developing practical, data‑driven solutions to improve audit processes.
Key Attributes for Success in Internal Audit
Assurance-focused mindset.
Strong understanding of how data is created, transformed, stored, governed, and consumed.
Ability to think end-to-end across the data lifecycle.
Curiosity to investigate data anomalies and root causes.
Strong documentation discipline and audit trail awareness.
Ability to bridge technical data engineering concepts and Internal Audit assurance requirements.
Strong attention to detail and professional scepticism.
Ability to link data anomalies to audit risks and internal control implications.
Methodical, well‑documented approach to ensure audit work is repeatable and defensible.
Collaborative mindset with a service orientation toward the Internal Audit team.
Ability to think “upstream” about how data is created, transformed, and governed, not only how it is analysed.

Join Lactalis South Africa, a global leader in the dairy industry, at our Ladismith Plant as a Food Safety Specialist. Your duties will include following up on corrective actions, identifying and mitigating potential food safety risks, and assisting in control procedures to ensure compliance with quality standards. Ideal candidates will have a minimum of 5 years' experience in dairy manufacturing, strong knowledge of supplier auditing and management systems, and expertise in microbiology and analytical chemistry. Join our dedicated team at Lactalis South Africa in Ladismith and contribute to delivering safe, high-quality dairy products that delight consumers worldwide.
Required Skills
Proven expertise in laboratory management within the food industry, ensuring compliance with Lactalis procedures and global quality standards.
Extensive knowledge and practical experience in implementing and auditing food safety management systems, including FSSC 22000 and HACCP.
Proficient in conducting internal and external audits, with a track record of supporting customer audits (e.g., Woolworths) and regulatory inspections by authorities such as the Department of Agriculture.
Strong analytical skills in managing raw milk quality data, collaborating closely with operational teams to drive continuous improvement initiatives.
Demonstrated ability to manage laboratory budgets effectively, optimizing costs and resource allocation to support business objectives.
Excellent leadership and cross-functional collaboration skills, facilitating industrial projects, root cause analyses, process improvements, and KPI achievement across quality, industrial, and maintenance teams.
In-depth understanding of hygiene, cleaning, and sanitation protocols, including CIP process validation and adherence to established cleaning schedules.
Experience coordinating export certification and audits, ensuring compliance with export regulations and prompt resolution of any audit findings.
Bachelor's degree or higher in Food Science, Microbiology, Chemistry, or a related field, supported by substantial relevant industry experience.
Strong communication and interpersonal abilities, capable of escorting auditors, engaging multiple stakeholders, and effectively managing customer complaint resolutions.

Oversee all laboratory operations to ensure strict adherence to Lactalis standard procedures and global quality standards.
Implement and sustain food safety management systems, including FSSC 22000 and HACCP, coordinating regular internal and external audits to maintain certification and compliance.
Lead external customer audits and regulatory inspections, ensuring preparedness and successful audit outcomes.
Collaborate with operational teams to monitor raw milk quality, perform root cause analysis, and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
Manage laboratory budgets effectively, including external testing and audit-related expenditures.
Coordinate hygiene and sanitization validation programs, ensuring compliance with Master Cleaning Schedules and cross-departmental standards.
Support cross-functional projects and quality improvement efforts by providing leadership and facilitating problem-solving activities.
Administer export certification processes and audits, ensuring all documentation and submissions comply with export regulations.
Conduct internal audits to identify training opportunities and promote a culture of quality and continuous development within the plant.
Liaise with external auditors, address customer quality complaints promptly, and implement corrective actions to minimize non-quality losses.

Support telecoms hardware including Yealink handsets, DECT devices and headsets.
Troubleshoot broadband, mobile broadband and leased-line connectivity.
Diagnose router, switch, Wi-Fi and LAN-related faults.
Analyse call quality, connectivity and service issues and identify root causes.
Manage technical faults from initial logging through to resolution within SLA.
Escalate complex technical faults appropriately.

Maintain accurate technical fault notes and customer updates.
Participate in ongoing technical and product training.

Matric.
Relevant Telecoms / Networking / Technical qualification advantageous.
Strong telephone-based technical support experience.
Proven troubleshooting experience across VoIP, IPPBX, internet connectivity and networks.
Yeastar experience is essential.
Good understanding of routers, switches, Wi-Fi and LAN environments.
Experience troubleshooting telecoms hardware and connectivity faults.
Strong fault diagnosis and logical problem-solving ability.
Able to take ownership of technical issues through to resolution.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Willing and able to work UK hours, including weekend shifts.
Position is full-time and office-based in Milnerton.
Advantageous
Previous experience within a telecommunications provider, ISP or VoIP environment.
Experience supporting UK-based customers.
Familiarity with South African ISPs and fibre providers such as MWEB, RSAWEB and Octotel.
Experience with 3CX, Bicom, IPECS, Yealink and DECT technologies.
